1_evidence_strength: Uses 3 primary studies, the national survey's raw table and clearly stated denominators, with section, table and page locations given. Spot-checks matched. It misses the one primary study of first-time users and leans on many C-grade news re-citations.
2_premise_testing: Tests 'text too small' with a within-subject comparison across steps (same people, same text) and a same-question ranking. A triangulation table gives support, out-of-scope and contradicting evidence for the premise and for rival claims. It also warns that the 7-point gap does not make a meaningful ranking.
약 245명 기준으로 세 비율의 차이는 7%p 안쪽이어서 순위 자체에 큰 의미를 두기는 어렵다
3_problem_location: Puts success rates (n=10) on 8 concrete steps and marks the steps with no evidence as empty. The 11-step order is borrowed from a cafe kiosk and labeled as assumed, and the participants were experienced users.
옵션(20~40%), 수량 바꾸기(40%), 담은 것 빼기(30%)에서 성공률이 절반 아래로 떨어졌다
4_insight_quality: Non-obvious points (the queue turns a stall into giving up; a franchise controls consistency across stores; help may itself be how people learn), each with an evidence grade and a caveat. The causal inference that step gaps rule out text is too strong: the young group also scored only 50% on add-ons, and text could interact with step difficulty.
글씨가 주된 원인이라면 단계별 차이가 이만큼 크게 벌어지기 어렵다
5_reframe_opportunity: Five lenses each tied to 'which decision changes'. The reframe keeps text size as one condition. The HMWs trace to the insights and expose a goal-definition decision ('zero staff calls' vs 'finishes alone'). Five HMWs is somewhat diffuse.
목표를 '직원 호출 0'으로 볼지, '막혀도 혼자 끝냄'으로 볼지 — 사람의 결정
6_principles_directions: Ten principles, each with evidence IDs, exceptions and conflicts. P6 is flagged as resting on guidelines only. Directions name order of work, what is lost, and %/s/count metrics. P10 ('keep payment as is') is never checked against evidence that first-timers did not know payment was in progress.
P6 ... 대상 집단 관찰 근거 없음(D·C만)
7_honesty_limits: Tags measured, inferred and speculative claims throughout. Labels the assumed structure, inferred denominator, sources it could not open, and missing domain coverage. One wrong statement: it says no primary first-time stepwise study exists, but that reflects a search gap, not invention.
이 순서는 카페 키오스크 기준의 가정한 구조이며 ... 처음 쓰는 손님은 더 낮을 수 있다. [추측]

1_evidence_strength: Core evidence is a primary observation of 8 genuine first-time users aged 62-83, cited precisely (Table 6/7/8/11/12). Spot-checks matched exactly. But nearly everything rests on that one study plus abstracts and news, and the 51.0% 'next button' figure comes only from an English news re-citation.
2_premise_testing: Compares the premise with a ranked Likert table (n=11) and survey rankings, and admits the gap is under 0.3. There is no independent triangulation, and it never brings in step-level counter-evidence (for example, other studies finding most failures at the option step).
점수 차이는 5점 척도에서 0.3점 안쪽이고 두 관찰 연구는 참여자가 4~11명
3_problem_location: Pins observed counts (4/8, 5/8, 8/8, 2) to concrete elements: the start button vs the ad, the category tab, the card reader. Honestly marks the option step as having no evidence, but that leaves the option and edit step (which other evidence shows is weak) as a blind spot.
8명 중 4명이 시작 방법을 찾지 못했다. 5명은 상단 광고에 시선을 빼앗겼다
4_insight_quality: Payment-feedback uncertainty is a valuable non-obvious finding. Insight 2 ('longest time') confuses task length with difficulty. Insights rest on one 8-person study, and Insight 3 has no caveat.
관찰한 8명 전원이 결제가 진행 중인지 알지 못했고 일부는 도중에 카드를 뺐다
5_reframe_opportunity: The reframe ('know the one next action; be sure payment finished') follows directly from the three stall points. Each HMW maps to one insight and one direction, and the directions change concrete screens. Queue pressure and help paths are deferred with no plan.
화면마다 다음에 할 일 하나를 알고, 결제가 끝났다고 확신하게 한다
6_principles_directions: Principles are concrete and traceable to tables. But one says 'no exception found', the metrics are vague (no targets or baseline), there is no explicit work order or trade-off among directions, and Principle 5 rests on a guideline plus one interview.
7_honesty_limits: Limitations section and 기록/해석/가설 tags are present. But the headline problem statement makes an untagged causal claim from n=8, and 'all five principles come from observed stalls or public guidelines' overstates. It does not disclose that most findings come from a single study.
처음 쓰는 60대 이상 손님은 글씨가 작아서보다 다음에 누를 곳과 결제가 끝났는지를 알 수 없어서 멈춘다.

overall: A is stronger analytically. It tests HQ's premise in two ways: a within-subject comparison (same people, same text, success ranging from 20% to 90%) and a triangulation table that separates support, incomparable scope and contradiction. Its denominators, evidence grades and statistical caution (a gap under 7 points is not a ranking) are more careful, and its principles and directions carry exceptions, work order and measurable metrics. B has the better single source (a genuine first-time-user observation with precise table references, verified accurate) and a tight insight-to-direction chain. But it builds almost everything on one 8-person study, has no triangulation, and states its causal headline without a tag. Neither report reconciles the conflict between A's 90% payment success and B's 8/8 not knowing payment was in progress. A's conclusion is also weakened because it missed B's first-time-user study.

A: When a population qualifier is in the brief (for example 'first-time'), weight the evidence by that match. Do not let a study of experienced users (EV-01) carry the main step-level claim. Before declaring the evidence absent, make an explicit search for qualifier-matched primary studies.

Do not draw a causal 'X is not the cause' from variation across steps unless confounds are ruled out: task difficulty for all ages (the young group scored 50% on add-ons) and text size or density differing by step.

A principle that says 'keep what works' must be checked against contrary evidence for the same step from other sources, for example payment success vs first-timers not knowing payment was in progress.
Rank and prune principles and HMWs by evidence weight. A long list of evenly presented items (10 principles, 5 HMWs) blurs the top priority.
B: Triangulate every headline claim across at least two independent primary sources. Disclose when most findings come from a single study and an n under 10.

When testing the client's premise, actively look for evidence that contradicts your own reframe as well as evidence against the premise. Handle the 'no data' steps (options and edits) as open risks to investigate, not as a lack of problems.
Do not read duration as difficulty. 'Took longest' can reflect task length. Use failure counts or a per-step baseline.

Tag the headline problem statement with its evidence level. Give each direction a baseline, a target, an explicit order of work and its trade-offs. Never write 'no exception found' without saying how exceptions were looked for.
